_comment: Curated static content set — intentionally NOT LLM-generated. Hand-authored against WHO/ICMR preventive-health guidelines. Using static data rather than a live AI call for three reasons: (1) zero API cost and latency on every page load, (2) content is human-reviewed and stable, (3) avoids risk of the model producing numeric targets, medication names, or diagnostic claims in a patient-facing UI. Update this file manually when guidance changes.
goals: Drink at least 6 glasses of water today and eat one extra serving of vegetables at a meal.
Take a 20-minute walk at a comfortable pace — morning or evening, wherever suits you.
Choose a whole-grain option (oats, brown rice, or whole-wheat bread) for one meal today.
Add one fruit to your breakfast or as a snack — any variety counts.
Replace one packaged or fried snack today with a handful of nuts, seeds, or fresh fruit.
Stand up and stretch for 5 minutes every hour if you have a desk-based day.
Cook or eat at least one home-prepared meal today — home cooking is a powerful preventive habit.
facts: Washing hands with soap for 20 seconds before meals and after using the toilet prevents a wide range of infections, including diarrhoeal diseases that cause millions of preventable deaths each year (WHO).
Regular moderate physical activity — such as brisk walking — reduces the risk of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, and several cancers (WHO Global Action Plan on Physical Activity).
A diet rich in fruits, vegetables, legumes, and whole grains provides fibre and micronutrients that support immune function and reduce chronic-disease risk (ICMR Dietary Guidelines for Indians).
Tobacco use — including smokeless tobacco — is the single largest preventable cause of cancer in India; stopping at any age brings measurable health benefits within months (ICMR).
Getting vaccinated according to your national schedule protects not just you but also people around you who cannot be vaccinated — including newborns and immunocompromised individuals (WHO).
Most adults need 7–9 hours of sleep per night; consistently poor sleep is linked to higher risk of hypertension, obesity, and reduced immune response (WHO).
Unmanaged stress raises cortisol levels and can worsen blood pressure, digestion, and immunity — simple breathing exercises and social support are evidence-based first-line strategies (ICMR).
tips: Keep a reusable water bottle visible at your desk or workspace — a visible cue significantly increases daily water intake.
Prepare a mixed vegetable sabzi or salad in bulk at the start of the week so healthy food is always the easiest choice.
Schedule any routine preventive check-ups (blood pressure, blood sugar, eye test) that you have been postponing — early detection saves lives.
Store fruits and pre-cut vegetables at eye level in your refrigerator so they are the first thing you see when you open it.
Walk or use stairs instead of a lift or auto-rickshaw for short distances — incidental movement adds up across the day.
Read food labels before buying packaged food — look at sodium and saturated fat content, not just calories.
If you smoke or use tobacco, speak to a doctor or call the national quit-line (1800-11-2356) — every attempt at quitting increases the likelihood of permanent cessation.
